solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Share price estimate cut before third quarter of year (5)

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its end
the first piece comes ahead of the second
a four-letter word's third quarter is its third letter

blocks.note: a QUOTE (price estimate) with its last letter cut
YEAR has four letters, so its third quarter is its third letter, A

annotation.surface: A financial note: a share-price forecast trimmed ahead of the year's third quarter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Third quarter' sounds like a business reporting period, but here it cuts the four-letter YEAR into quarters and takes the third one.
annotation.definitionFit: A quota is a person's allotted share of something.

entries.clue: Weapon found in army accommodation mostly by servants (12)

indicators.note: most of the word, so drop its last letter
the next piece sits beside it

blocks.note: QUARTERS, where soldiers are lodged, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A weapon turns up in the soldiers' lodgings, near where the servants live.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found in' reads like a container instruction, but it only links the definition to the wordplay, which is a simple sequence.
annotation.definitionFit: A quarterstaff is a long wooden pole used as a weapon in old English combat.

entries.clue: Come about dog chasing round about (5)

indicators.note: one who chases comes behind, so CUR goes after the other pieces

blocks.note: O is round in shape, and C = circa, about
a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: A dog runs round and round after something, and then things happen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' appears twice with different jobs: the first belongs to the definition 'Come about', the second is the abbreviation C for circa.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things that come about are said to occur, both meaning happen.

entries.clue: Angers friend and declines to accept quiet place on board (9)

indicators.note: DIPS takes SH inside itself

blocks.note: in Angers, a French city, a friend is an ami

annotation.surface: Someone angers a friend and refuses to accept a quiet spot aboard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Angers' is not a verb but the French city on the Loire, so its friend is the French AMI; the capital letter at the clue's start hides this.
annotation.definitionFit: Amidships names a location: the middle part of a vessel, so a place on board in the nautical sense.

entries.clue: Father left holding unruly steed as mount (8)

indicators.note: PA L holds the other letters inside
the letters of STEED behave badly and scatter

blocks.note: STEED rearranged, placed between P and A

annotation.surface: A father on the left clings to an unruly horse he is trying to ride.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'mount' a horse to ride, fitting the steed; the answer is a mount in the other sense, something a statue stands on.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or mount on which a statue or column stands.

entries.clue: Call to limit length for fabric (6)

indicators.note: POP IN goes round L, bounding it

blocks.note: to pop in is to call on someone briefly

annotation.surface: A demand to restrict how much fabric is used.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Call' must be read as a visit, POP IN, not a shout or phone call.
annotation.definitionFit: Poplin is a plain-woven cotton fabric.

entries.clue: Moving Perseids vanish (8)

indicators.note: the letters of PERSEIDS change position

annotation.surface: Shooting stars of the Perseid shower streak across the sky and disappear.
annotation.walkthrough: The Perseids are an August meteor shower, so 'moving' and 'vanish' both fit the surface of meteors burning up.
annotation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter and so vanish from sight, as a crowd or mist does.

entries.clue: Small child trapping a wild animal (5)

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it caught inside, so TOT closes round A

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a tot is a small child

annotation.surface: A little child manages to catch a wild creature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small child' reads as one phrase, but it splits: S and TOT.
annotation.definitionFit: A stoat is a small wild carnivore of the weasel family.

entries.clue: Mortification from losing some database mentions (9)

indicators.note: the phrase sheds some letters at each end, leaving the answer inside

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words, with three letters dropped at the front and four at the back

annotation.surface: Someone is embarrassed after losing records from a database.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, dat-ABASE MENT-ions, so it is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the humiliation of being brought low.

entries.clue: Brandy locked up by principal that is friend of top cleric (14)

indicators.note: PISCO is shut inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: arch = chief, principal, as in archenemy
pisco is a grape brandy from Peru and Chile

annotation.surface: Brandy is kept locked away by a headteacher who is friendly with the archbishop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Friend of top cleric' wants to be the definition, but 'friend' is PAL; 'of top cleric' is the adjective, and 'principal' is ARCH, not a headteacher.
annotation.definitionFit: Archiepiscopal means relating to an archbishop, the top cleric.

entries.clue: Peer admitted working thought out in advance (12)

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new order

annotation.surface: A lord confesses that he was working to a plan made beforehand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Admitted' looks like a container instruction but is part of the fodder, with 'working' as the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Premeditated means planned or thought out beforehand.

entries.clue: Way to enter word game letter after several goes? (9)

indicators.note: after means following in time or order, so TILE is written following TURNS

blocks.note: in Scrabble each letter is on a tile

annotation.surface: A question of how to join in a word game: your letter comes after several rounds of play.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scrabble setting makes 'goes' look like more game play, which it is, but in the sense of TURNS.
annotation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a rotating gate through which people enter a stadium or station.

entries.clue: Who collected taxes belonging to them (5)

blocks.note: the Inland Revenue, Britain's tax collector until 2005, abbreviated and given its article

annotation.surface: A question about who used to gather taxes owed by them.
annotation.walkthrough: THE IR is the Inland Revenue, merged into HMRC in 2005, hence the past tense 'collected'.
annotation.definitionFit: A possessive pronoun: their stands in for 'belonging to them' before a noun.

entries.clue: Movement of vehicles stripped a palm tree (6)

indicators.note: the word loses its outer layer, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Passing traffic has stripped the leaves off a palm tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' seems to act on the palm tree, but it strips TRAFFIC.
annotation.definitionFit: The raffia is a palm whose leaf fibre is used for weaving and tying.

entries.clue: Endless anger being immersed in our neighbour’s perfume (9)

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter
RAG goes under, inside FRANCE

blocks.note: France is Britain's nearest neighbour across the Channel

annotation.surface: Someone is furious at being dunked in French perfume.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Our' is the British setter's viewpoint: Britain's neighbour is France.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fragrance is a pleasant scent, and a perfume is one bottled.

entries.clue: Line on map is different motorway (8)

blocks.note: M, as in M1, marks a British motorway

annotation.surface: A line shown on a road map turns out to be another motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: The road-map surface makes the line a route, but it is a weather-map line; 'is' is simply part of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line on a map joining places of equal temperature.

entries.clue: Fruit with sharp flavour, one eaten by bird (9)

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so I goes inside ERNE

blocks.note: a tang is a sharp taste
the erne is a sea eagle

annotation.surface: A tart piece of fruit gets pecked by a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bird eating fruit, but the thing eaten is the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange citrus fruit.

entries.clue: When uncovered, cops spot one’s onto rival (8)

indicators.note: each word has its covering, the first and last letters, taken off

annotation.surface: Once exposed, police notice someone going after a competitor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' sounds like being found out, but it strips the outer letters from each of the next four words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an opponent is the one on the other side, which is what a rival is.

entries.clue: Managed a month in teetotal part of religious institution (8)

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so RAN and SEP sit within TT

blocks.note: SEP is the calendar abbreviation for September

annotation.surface: Someone ran a month of abstinence as part of a religious order's rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Religious institution' suggests a monastery or order, but here it is a church building.
annotation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church.

entries.clue: One not ready to print when an editor’s absent (6)

definitions.note: 'One' is used as an adjective, as in 'we are one'

indicators.note: ED is missing from the word

blocks.note: copy not yet edited is not ready to print
ED = editor; this is what goes

annotation.surface: A newspaper page cannot go to press because the editor is away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a noun for a person, but it means joined together, united.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: people who are 'one' in purpose are united, joined as a single body.

entries.clue: Lack of movement in street in current circumstances (6)

blocks.note: as is = in its present state

annotation.surface: Traffic in the street is at a standstill under present conditions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In current circumstances' reads as a throwaway phrase but is the whole of AS IS.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed Greek term: stasis means standing still, a state where nothing moves.

entries.clue: Fancy involving Royal Artillery unit (5)

indicators.note: to involve is to include or take in, so FAD takes RA inside

blocks.note: a fad is a passing fancy
the initials of Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

annotation.surface: A passing craze sweeps through an army artillery unit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unit' reads as a military unit next to the Royal Artillery, but it is a unit of measurement.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the farad is a unit, the SI measure of electrical capacitance named after Faraday.

entries.clue: Golf club’s not very short of water by comparison? (5)

indicators.note: the next item is to be left out

blocks.note: the driver is the club for long tee shots
V = very; this is what goes

annotation.surface: A remark that a golf club is hardly any shorter than one would like.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short' pairs with 'very' in the surface, but it belongs to the definition; the question mark flags that 'short of water' is a playful way to say dry.
annotation.definitionFit: Drier means having less water than something else, short of water by comparison.

entries.clue: Old actor entering not at the place specified (2,3,4)

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so THESP goes into NOT

blocks.note: thesp, short for thespian, an actor
taken as written; THESP enters after its N

annotation.surface: An elderly actor comes on, but not where he was supposed to be.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old actor' reads as one phrase, a veteran performer, but splits into O and THESP.
annotation.definitionFit: On the spot means at the very place in question.

entries.clue: Feeling of regret concealing river accident (5)

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide from view within, so PANG hides R inside

annotation.surface: Someone feels guilty about hiding a mishap at the river.
annotation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
annotation.definitionFit: A prang is a crash or accident, especially a minor one in a vehicle.

entries.clue: It pains partner to adjust to something meaning “no sweat” (14)

indicators.note: the letters are adjusted into a new order

annotation.surface: A spouse finds it painful to get used to something that means 'no problem'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No sweat' is slang for 'no trouble'; the definition takes it literally.
annotation.definitionFit: An antiperspirant prevents sweating, so it literally means no sweat.

entries.clue: Rubbish has duster frantic around it (8)

indicators.note: the letters of DUSTER are thrown into disorder
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go on either side of IT

annotation.surface: Someone flaps a duster wildly around the debris.
annotation.walkthrough: The cleaning scene makes 'duster' look like a tool, but it is only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: detritus is debris, the loose waste left over, which is rubbish.

entries.clue: Gradually pushed border back to Scotland (5)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: An army slowly pushed the frontier back towards Scotland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border' and 'Scotland' suggest the Anglo-Scottish border, and 'back' a retreat, but 'back to' simply means the end of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: To edge something is to push it gradually, a little at a time.
